question.problem: Determine the horizontal asymptote of the function $f(x)=\frac{7{x}^{2}+4}{x(3{x}^{2}+12)}.$
question.worked_solution:
The given function can be rewritten as follows:

$$
f(x)=\frac{7{x}^{2}+4}{3{x}^{3}+12x}
$$

To find the horizontal asymptote of a rational function, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by the dominant term in the denominator, and then we let $x\to \infty .$

Ignoring the coefficient, the dominant term in the denominator is ${x}^{3}.$ So, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by ${x}^{3},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{7{x}^{2}+4}{3{x}^{3}+12x} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{7{x}^{2}}{{x}^{3}}+\frac{4}{{x}^{3}})}{(\frac{3{x}^{3}}{{x}^{3}}+\frac{12x}{{x}^{3}})} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{7}{x}+\frac{4}{{x}^{3}})}{(3+\frac{12}{{x}^{2}})}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, when $x$ is very large, the terms $\frac{7}{x},\frac{4}{{x}^{3}}$ and $\frac{12}{{x}^{2}}$ become very small. Therefore, as $x\to \infty ,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{(\frac{7}{x}+\frac{4}{{x}^{3}})}{(3+\frac{12}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & \to \frac{0+0}{3+0} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the horizontal asymptote is $y=0.$
